title: You think God is punishing you.
paragraphs: You think God is punishing you.

But what if…
He’s exposing what you’ve been hiding?
That whisper in your chest when everything started falling apart.

Maybe because of that secret.
That compromise.
That thing no one knows… but God does.
And suddenly, life doesn’t just hurt—
Trying to answer the question that won’t leave you alone:
But here’s the tension nobody talks about:

What if your suffering isn’t proof of your guilt…
but a battlefield for your faith?

They saw his pain—
and assumed his sin.

They saw his losses—
and concluded his failure.

We look at broken marriages…
and whisper, “They must have messed up.”

We see someone lose everything…
and think, “God is correcting them.”

We experience pain ourselves…
and immediately go:
“And the LORD said to Satan, ‘Have you considered my servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil?’”
So what does that mean for you?
It means your pain is not always a verdict.
Not a reveal of your sin—
But a reveal of your trust.
Because when everything is stripped away—
That’s where the real battle is.
And Job stood in that place.
“Though He slay me, yet will I trust Him.”
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
But some suffering exposes what we’ve been avoiding.
“When I kept silent, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long. For day and night your hand was heavy on me…”
Some storms don’t come to test you—
They come to turn you back.
And that’s where shame steps in.
Shame doesn’t just say, “You did wrong.”
“But the LORD God called to the man, ‘Where are you?’ He answered, ‘I heard you… and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid.’”
That’s the first symptom of shame:
And maybe that’s you right now.

Still attending church.
Still posting verses.
Still smiling.

“If God really saw everything…
He wouldn’t want me.”
But here’s the truth that breaks that lie:
This is where Job points forward.
“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
Jesus became what you’re ashamed of—
So you could become what you could never earn.
“But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on Him…”
So if you are in Christ—
He may be calling you deeper.
That was settled at the cross.
“Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
So what do you do with your suffering now?
You stop interpreting it through shame—
And start anchoring it in truth.
If there is no clear sin—
Because the same God who allowed Job’s testing—
Is the same God who restored him.
“The LORD restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as he had before.”
And the same God who allowed the cross—
Is the God who raised Jesus from the dead.
But it will not stay there.
Say it if you mean it:
He is not waiting to crush you.
He is ready to receive you.
